_comment: Clarivate's own names for the schemes this site filters by, each with a link
to Clarivate's own definition. A reader who wants to know what a facet means
should get the answer from the people who made it, not from us paraphrasing.
Names are the field labels as they appear in the Categories/Classification
block of a Web of Science record, not our shortenings of them. All three
schemes are Clarivate's and all three were read from Web of Science.
basis is the thing worth teaching. A venue-based scheme classifies the
journal or proceedings volume, and every paper in it inherits the same
answer. A paper-based scheme classifies the individual record. They disagree
often and both are correct — our IJCAI paper is Computer Science by venue and
Chemistry by citation, because it was published at an AI conference but cites
and is cited by molecular science.
labels is what a paper can carry: 'multi' means it appears under every value
that applies, 'single' means exactly one. Multi-label fails safe for browsing
— nothing hides in a bucket the reader did not think to open.
The Citation Topics link is Clarivate's official documentation but sits
behind a bot check that blocked automated verification, so it was not loaded
end to end. It resolves normally in a browser.

wos-subject-categories.name: Web of Science Categories
wos-subject-categories.summary: Clarivate assigns these to the journal or proceedings volume. Every paper published there inherits them.
wos-subject-categories.note: Clarivate's help article titles this "Web of Science Subject Categories"; the field label on a record reads "Web of Science Categories". We show the record label, since that is what a reader matching against Web of Science will see.

research-areas.name: Research Areas
research-areas.summary: A fixed roll-up of the subject categories, shared across every Web of Science database so records from different databases can be compared.

citation-topics.name: Citation Topics
citation-topics.summary: Built by clustering the citation network rather than by classifying journals, so a paper lands with the literature it actually cites and is cited by. Developed by Clarivate with CWTS Leiden. Each paper gets exactly one micro topic, which rolls up to one meso and one macro.
citation-topics.note: Official Clarivate documentation; automated verification was blocked by a bot check, not by a broken link.

document-types.name: Document Types
document-types.summary: What kind of record it is — Article, Review, Proceedings Paper, Book Chapter.

core-collection.name: Web of Science Core Collection
core-collection.summary: The indexes these classifications come from: SCIE, SSCI, AHCI, ESCI for journals and CPCI for conference proceedings. A paper absent from the Core Collection carries none of these values.
